messages:
jamie: Heads up — our strict fncall validator canary (slice=prod-delta) started rejecting ~1.2% of tool invocations. Clients fell back to freeform text which broke downstream tooling. Noticed in error-rate spike around 11:12 PST.
sana: saw it too. I pulled a sample from logs: `validator: field 'result.items' expected object got array`. Example payload attached below.
sana: ```json
{"tool":"search","response":{"result":{"items":["a","b"]}}}
```
omar: thanks. Was the canary set to fail-fast? That's the big change vs soft-validate.
jamie: yes, canary = strict mode, fail-fast. We shipped to 10% and it hit some real traffic patterns.
tess: this is expected but we didn't have an easy signal in console — only error counts. We should add a per-route 'fncall acceptance rate' and top-5 failure reasons.
priya: also to point out: customers were re-issuing requests when they saw bad outputs, which doubled token usage in a few cases. Are rejected fncalls currently billed? We should decide asap.
omar: currently yes, billing happens at request acceptance time. If validator rejects and we fallback, we still bill for LLM generation tokens. We can change classification but need product approval.
ralph: SRE note: if we mark rejects non-billable, operator-scripts might be gamed. propose: non-billable only for automatic soft-fallbacks where strictness=canary and we observed canonical output loss, and only counted if sample evidence exists.
eve-ml: alternative: introduce 'soft-validate' mode which returns the original fncall but includes `validation:{ok:false, reason:"schema_mismatch"}` metadata in response. Console can show examples, but producers still get full payload so no silent breakage.
jamie: I like soft-validate for canary. It avoids user-visible break while giving ops data. Need to ensure adapters/tooling can ignore `validation` metadata.
sana: implement telemetry: new metric `fncall.validation.result` labels: model, route, failure_reason, mode(canary|prod), strictness(strict|soft). Sample bodies at 0.5% with PII redaction.
tess: Console work: UI card per-route with acceptance %, top failure reasons, sample payload viewer with redaction toggle, and a rollout helper that suggests switching canary from strict -> soft -> strict with step sizes.
priya: on billing: propose not to change retroactive billing now. For canaries mark 'fncall_failure_billing="no"' for known canary runids and surface in invoice notes. Product to confirm.
jamie: action items:
- @omar add metric + labels to telemetry pipeline (owner: omar) 
- @eve-ml prototype soft-validate payload flag and adapter compatibility test (owner: eve-ml)
- @tess mock console card and rollout UX (owner: tess)
- @priya sync with product on billing semantics (owner: priya)
- @sana add sampler + redaction to log exporter (owner: sana)

deploy-bot: canary strict-validator rollback initiated by jamie at 11:48 PST :rotating_light:
jamie: thanks. we'll roll soft-validate to canary then re-run metrics. Keep thread updated.
omar: quick thought — add a 'schema_reject_backoff' policy in routing: if a client hits N rejects in M minutes, route to permissive variant for next K minutes to avoid retry storms.
tess: agree, add to routing policies doc. I'll create a small RFC and link in this thread.
priya: filed product ticket #IN-4237 for billing/UX followup.
jamie: perfect. closing this loop. ping me if you need access to the samples bucket.
